//: `checkJs` runs the TypeScript compiler over the existing .js files. No file
is renamed, no syntax changes, nothing ships differently — `noEmit` means it
only ever reports, never writes. Types come from three places already in the
project: the JSDoc comments written throughout, the .d.ts files that ship
with every dependency, and the types Prisma generates from schema.prisma.
That last one is the real prize. `prisma.formSubmission.findMany()` is fully
typed from the schema, so a typo in a column name or a wrong `include` is
caught here rather than at 3am in production.
WHY NOT A FULL MIGRATION: 123 files and ~28k lines, days of work, every file
touched, right before deployment — with 116 passing tests to put at risk.
This catches the same classes of bug today at a fraction of the cost, and
leaves a real migration possible later, file by file.
//include: prisma/seed-data holds literal data — TypeScript infers its object shapes
from the first entry and then objects to every later one that has an extra
key, producing ~120 findings that are all noise.
scripts/ drives the API loosely on purpose (it pokes at responses to prove
they are wrong), which is exactly the shape a type-checker complains about.
Excluding both keeps the signal in src/, where a finding means something.
They are still covered by ESLint, which is the check that matters for them.
